name: flatulence

phase_0.boundary_condition: the gastrointestinal tract and anal canal

VINIT.justification: the absence of gas before fermentation begins

TANCH.justification: the final boundary where the gas merges with the external environment

AFWD.justification: the directed movement of gas toward the exit

AREV.justification: the reverse movement or reabsorption of gas into the blood

CLINK.justification: the sequential breakdown of carbohydrates into gaseous byproducts

IMSCRIB.justification: the internal recognition of pressure as a distinct sensation

FSPLIT.justification: the separation of the gas volume into potential release or retention paths

FFUSE.justification: the restoration of the baseline abdominal state regardless of the path taken

EVALF.justification: the suppression of release and maintenance of internal pressure

ENGAGR.justification: the simultaneous urge to evacuate and the inability to do so effectively

phase_3.both_description: the state of holding gas while feeling the urge to release

steps.domain_action: bacteria metabolize complex sugars into hydrogen and methane
the enteric nervous system identifies the presence of a gas pocket
peristaltic waves push the gas toward the rectum
the internal sphincter encounters the gas and initiates a choice
the external sphincter relaxes to allow passage
the gas enters the atmosphere and leaves a scent record
the rectal vault returns to its empty state
a second gas pocket arrives at the junction
social constraints force the external sphincter to remain closed
the gas moves back into the sigmoid colon
the rectal vault returns to its empty state
a third gas pocket arrives with ambiguous density
the system cannot distinguish between gas and liquid matter
the system remains in a state of cautious tension
the gas eventually dissipates into the surrounding air

phase_6.post_cycle_state: low internal pressure and atmospheric equilibrium
